body:
## Problem

The ui2 ruler no longer is a (left-aligned) box of fixed width, but the remnants of ui1 still unnecessarily constrain the ruler to a maximum width. This width is configured by reusing the item group syntax in an inconsistent way, which causes a number of surprising edge-cases. The inconsistencies have become more apparent when the C implementation of the statusline was replaced with a default expression in 0.12, since it reuses the ruler as an expression instead of pre-rendered. And also, because the fixed width, which was configured in the `minwid` position, is now a de-facto maximum width. Furthermore, `v:echospace` is still set according to the old rules.

## Solution

Remove arbitrary constraints and process item groups in `rulerformat` the same as in all the other statusline-style options. The current fallback ruler expression in the default `statusline` (`%-14.(%l,%c%V%)\ %P`) now actually works for `rulerformat` itself, even with different `minwid` values and both with or without the period.

Deprecate `v:echospace`, since it's main purpose was to avoid "Press ENTER" prompts, which ui2 was designed to get rid of, and it would add undue complexity to ui2 to keep supporting it.

~Make ui2 itself responsible of setting `v:echospace` according to its layout of the last line. It must be updated whenever the ruler changes in size, e.g. when `rulerformat=%l` and the cursor moves from line 9 to line 10.
There are edge-cases with a flexible ruler when the command that evaluates `v:echospace` changes the ruler width.~

~I couldn't find any internal state that could simply be exposed as `v:echospace`. In particular, `messages.cmd.last_col` is related, but different: as far as I can tell, it tracks the current space allocated for a currently displayed message, which can fluctuate e.g. when search count or `showcmd` (dis)appear. But this is uninteresting for the purposes of `v:echospace`, which tracks the space available for newly appearing messages, and those write over any search count and are delayed until `showcmd` disappears again (this is another departure from ui1, where space is reserved for `showcmd` outside of `v:echospace`). I documented my current understanding of the cropping behaviour in the form of unit tests, except for an `echo` inside a multi-line/control-flow command, which I found difficult to test.~

I don't know if the breaking changes need mentioning in vim_diff.txt and/or news.txt, since ui2 is still experimental/unstable but was already mentioned as a new feature in news-0.12.txt.
The breaking changes from ui1 to ui2 are more interesting than those between beta versions of ui2, but they will probably be announced collectively when ui2 replaces ui1. Is news-breaking-dev the place to collect those?

Fix #40247

comment_data.body: This change seems redundant; `set_keep_msg()` already returns early with `ui_has(kUIMessages)`.
These changes seem only tangentially related, is there a regression test for this? Could do with a comment why the ext_messages branch is needed/useful or even a separate PR/commit?
Indeed, I didn't pay enough attention here.

Yes, I'll document this change in a comment and/or commit message. But I'm realising that it might need more discussion beforehand.

My intuition is that this part of the code shouldn't know about the exact message box dimensions at the receiving end, the UI should decide itself how to handle the message depending on its length, especially now that long messages are not really disruptive anymore.

EDIT: moved analysis into commit messages and code comments

In general, short messages (< 1 line) are not shown at all when INSERT/VISUAL/... mode or "-- Keyword completion..." is shown, because those elements begin at the far left of the cmdline, so that the messages is cropped to 0. Maybe it's a good idea to always expand the cmdline in such cases?
EDIT: sorry, this seems a bit off-topic, but I need to know what you think should happen to know how to handle this.
I think it's best to keep the messages below `Columns` for now. This avoids handling these questions in this PR.

ai claims there may be an overflow potential here. repro use "±" (which is 2 bytes)

```
:set fillchars=stl:±
:set statusline=%-1500000000(x%)
```

`added_bytes = 1.5e9*2` wraps negative

comment_regular_data.body: rebased onto master and added news

> Furthermore, v:echospace is still set according to the old rules

Can we not just drop this? Doesn't really make sense with ext_messages in the first place so maintaining it just for when the UI2 cmdline target is used, where overflow is supposed to be less disruptive than the hit-enter prompt seems unnecessary?

i suggest moving `v:echospace` to deprecated.txt in this PR. and remove most/all references to it throughout the docs.

ui2 is the way forward.

> i suggest moving `v:echospace` to deprecated.txt in this PR. and remove most/all references to it throughout the docs.

done

- rebased onto master
- created a separate commit for removing the obsolete usages of `sc_col` and triple-checked that I didn't miss anything
- explained the details in commit message and code comments
- still keeping the concerned messages under 1 line to avoid dealing with edge-cases that seem out of scope for this PR
- had to fix another glitch in ui2 related to repeated long messages, otherwise I would have had to keep the "match in file" messages under `Columns/2` to make sure they never reach the ruler (unfortunately, there was a complication related to textlock, which I don't fully understand)
